## Overview

IC-9 compute turn-down declaration: frozen contract, version 1.0.0 (roadmap WP-SITE-07, B8-01).

A GPU operator *declares* the turn-down its workloads can offer at one site: how many kW of IT load,
for how long, on how much notice, at what price, under which service-level class, and when.
Declaring is optional and never assumed (A2-04): with no declaration there is no instance, and the
data-centre load model leaves IT load untouched (spec §14, "IT load untouched" is the default).
Producer: the GPU operator, or an orchestrator adapter (WP-SITE-08, B8-02). Consumers: the
co-optimising sizer A5 (WP-SIZE-11), live dispatch B2 in shadow mode, IC-3, and the
data-centre load model's on-request turn-down overlay.

Spec → this contract (decisions D-NEW-SITE07-1 to -6):

=====================================  =======================================================
spec (§10A IC-9, B8-01)                field
=====================================  =======================================================
"MW"                                   ``envelopes[*].curve`` (`AbsoluteCurve` kW or
                                       `RelativeCurve` basis points of running IT load)
"duration"                             ``curve.points[*].max_hold_min``
"notice"                               ``envelopes[*].response`` (`ResponseTerms`, seconds)
"price"                                ``envelopes[*].price`` (`PriceOffer` or ``unknown``)
"SLA class"                            ``sla_classes`` (`SlaClass`), named by
                                       ``envelopes[*].sla_class_id``
"validity"                             ``valid_from``, ``valid_until`` (half-open),
                                       ``availability`` (the GB-clock template and dated
                                       overrides), ``resolved_hash``, ``supersedes``
=====================================  =======================================================

**Conditional, never firm floor.** A declared kW is the operator's commitment, but it is a
resource offered by a third party's workloads: every consumer classifies IC-9 kW as
CONDITIONAL (B8-03), outside the priced floor. The contract carries no firmness field and no
validator or reader refuses, zeroes or ranks a revenue stream (D57): the only rule it enforces
between offers is arithmetic, so the same kW is never counted twice (stacking, the shared
call budget of an SLA class, and the retained IT floor). Stage L4 is advisory and shadow only
(ADR-D2): there is no instruction or acknowledgement message in this version.

**Measured at IT load.** Every turn-down quantity is IT electrical load. What it saves at the
meter (UPS, distribution, cooling) is the load model's job (its turn-down overlay).

**Exact integers.** Power integer kW, shares integer basis points (1/10,000), hold durations
integer minutes (1 to `MAX_HOLD_MIN`), notice and ramp integer seconds, money integer pence.
A producer rounds to the safe side: kW, basis points and hold durations down, notice and ramp up,
and refuses rather than emits a zero offer.

**Time base.** A recurring template on the GB clock (`CLOCK`): ``seasons`` partition the months,
``day_groups`` partition the ISO week, 30-minute ``bands`` partition the local day, and each
cell's state is `Offered` (named envelopes), `Unavailable` (with a reason) or ``unknown``.
Dated UTC ``overrides`` on the half-hour grid replace the state wholesale. `resolve` compiles the
declaration onto UTC half-hours (`ResolvedTimeline`); ``resolved_hash`` binds that compilation,
so two implementations that read a clock change differently fail conformance instead of
disagreeing silently. `declared_at_local` reads the declaration at a naive local half-hour (the
load model's time basis) under PEP 495 ``fold=0``: on the spring-forward day the missing local
hour 01:00 to 02:00 reads UTC 01:00 to 02:00, which local 02:00 to 03:00 also reads; on the
fall-back day the repeated local hour is read at its first occurrence (BST).

Version: ``CONTRACT_VERSION`` (a ``Literal`` on every instance); JSON Schemas frozen at
``schemas/ic9_compute_turndown_declaration.v1.0.0.schema.json`` and
``schemas/ic9_resolved_timeline.v1.0.0.schema.json``; human-readable specification generated at
``specs/ic9_compute_turndown_declaration.v1.0.0.md``; git tag ``GIT_TAG``. References IC-4
evidence through `EvidenceRef` (the 1.x range).

## Schema `ic9_compute_turndown_declaration`

### `ComputeTurndownDeclaration`

IC-9 v1.0.0: the turn-down one GPU operator declares at one site over one validity. ``envelopes`` are the menu (sorted by ``envelope_id``), ``sla_classes`` the service classes they name (sorted by ``class_id``; each named by at least one envelope), ``availability`` says which envelopes are offered at every half-hour of ``[valid_from, valid_until)``, and ``resolved_hash`` binds its compilation (`resolve`). ``stacking`` and ``it_reference`` are the arithmetic that stops one kW being counted twice. Every envelope is offered somewhere.

| field | type | required | default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `availability` | `AvailabilityTemplate` | yes |  |
| `basis` | `DeclaredBasis` or `TrialledBasis` or `MeteredBasis` | yes |  |
| `clock` | `"Europe/London"` | yes |  |
| `contract` | `"IC-9"` | no | `"IC-9"` |
| `contract_version` | `"1.0.0"` | no | `"1.0.0"` |
| `declaration_id` | string; pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]*$` | yes |  |
| `envelopes` | array of `TurndownEnvelope`; items >= 1 | yes |  |
| `issued_at` | string (date-time) | yes |  |
| `it_reference` | `ItReference` | yes |  |
| `measurement_point` | `"it_load"` | yes |  |
| `operator_id` | string; length >= 1, pattern `\S` | yes |  |
| `record_class` | one of `"registered"`, `"synthetic_fixture"` | yes |  |
| `resolved_hash` | string; pattern `^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$` | yes |  |
| `site_id` | string; length >= 1, pattern `\S` | yes |  |
| `sla_classes` | array of `SlaClass`; items >= 1 | yes |  |
| `stacking` | `Stacking` | yes |  |
| `supersedes` | string; pattern `^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$` or `NotApplicable` | yes |  |
| `valid_from` | string (date-time) | yes |  |
| `valid_until` | string (date-time) | yes |  |

### `AvailabilityTemplate`

When each envelope is offered: the recurring GB-clock template and the dated overrides. ``seasons`` partition the months (sorted by first month), ``day_groups`` the ISO week (sorted by first weekday), ``bands`` the local day (sorted, contiguous, 0 to 1440). ``cells`` hold exactly one state per (season, day group, band), in that order, and the template is canonical: no two bands, day groups or seasons carry the same states everywhere.

| field | type | required | default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bands` | array of `TimeBand`; items >= 1 | yes |  |
| `cells` | array of `TemplateCell`; items >= 1 | yes |  |
| `day_groups` | array of `DayGroup`; items >= 1 | yes |  |
| `overrides` | array of `Override` | yes |  |
| `seasons` | array of `Season`; items >= 1 | yes |  |

| `ramp_s` | integer; >= 0 | yes |  |

### `SlaClass`

A service-level class, declared once and named by envelopes. ``operator_label`` is the operator's own name for it: opaque, never parsed, compared or ranked. ``workload_action`` constrains ``energy_return``: deferred work returns (not ``no_return``); moved or dropped work does not return here (not ``returns_later``); slowed work may do either. There is no rank and no firmness: protection is the absence of an envelope, and every IC-9 kW is CONDITIONAL to a consumer.

| field | type | required | default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `call_limits` | `CallLimits` | yes |  |

| `energy_return` | `ReturnsLater` or `NoReturn` or `Unknown` | yes |  |
| `operator_label` | string; length >= 1, length <= 200, pattern `\S` | yes |  |
| `sla_evidence` | `EvidenceRef` or `Unknown` | yes |  |
| `workload_action` | `WorkloadAction` or `Unknown` | yes |  |

### `UnavailableReason`

Why a cell or an override offers nothing (as distinct from ``unknown``).

Values: `workload_protected`, `outside_agreed_window`, `operator_withdrawn`, `maintenance`

### `Unknown`

A value that exists but is not known. Always explicit, always with a reason; never ``None``. Serialised as ``{"kind": "unknown", "reason": "..."}``. ``kind`` is required (no default) so a hand-written payload that omits it is refused rather than guessed at.

| field | type | required | default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `"unknown"` | yes |  |
| `reason` | string; length >= 1, pattern `\S` | yes |  |

| `kind` | `"utilisation_price"` | yes |  |
| `pence_per_mwh` | integer; >= 1 | yes |  |

### `WorkloadAction`

What the operator does to its workloads to turn down. Closed; a minor version extends it.

Values: `deferred`, `slowed`, `moved`, `dropped`

## Schema `ic9_resolved_timeline`

### `ResolvedTimeline`

IC-9 v1.0.0: a declaration's availability compiled onto UTC half-hours (`resolve`). Step-encoded: a step starts wherever the state or its origin changes. Read with no clock logic (`timeline_state_at`); trusted by ``content_hash() == declaration.resolved_hash``.

| field | type | required | default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `contract` | `"IC-9"` | no | `"IC-9"` |
| `contract_version` | `"1.0.0"` | no | `"1.0.0"` |
| `declaration_id` | string; pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]*$` | yes |  |
| `kind` | `"resolved_timeline"` | yes |  |
| `n_periods` | integer; >= 1 | yes |  |
| `resolution_min` | `30` | yes |  |
| `site_id` | string; length >= 1, pattern `\S` | yes |  |
| `steps` | array of `TimelineStep`; items >= 1 | yes |  |
| `valid_from` | string (date-time) | yes |  |
| `valid_until` | string (date-time) | yes |  |

### `Offered`

The named envelopes are offered (each envelope is a menu item; `stack_at` combines them).

| field | type | required | default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `envelope_ids` | array of string; pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]*$`; items >= 1 | yes |  |
| `kind` | `"offered"` | yes |  |

### `TimelineStep`

From ``start`` to the next step (or the validity's end), ``state`` holds, from the template or from a dated override (``origin``: a blackout and a template gap read differently).

| `state` | `Offered` or `Unavailable` or `Unknown` | yes |  |

### `Unavailable`

Nothing is offered, for a stated reason. A template cell reads as ``not_offered``; a dated override reads as ``blackout`` (`CallReason`).

Why a cell or an override offers nothing (as distinct from ``unknown``).

Values: `workload_protected`, `outside_agreed_window`, `operator_withdrawn`, `maintenance`

### `Unknown`

A value that exists but is not known. Always explicit, always with a reason; never ``None``. Serialised as ``{"kind": "unknown", "reason": "..."}``. ``kind`` is required (no default) so a hand-written payload that omits it is refused rather than guessed at.

| field | type | required | default |

## Readers

The contract's functions, each the one way to answer its question. Signatures are the module's own annotations.

### `active_at(declarations: 'Sequence[ComputeTurndownDeclaration]', instant: 'datetime') -> 'ComputeTurndownDeclaration | NotApplicable'`

The declaration in force at ``instant`` among one site's declarations (IC-3's rule).

### `availability_cost_pence(price: 'PriceOffer | Unknown', *, held_kw: 'int', held_min: 'int') -> 'Fraction | Unknown'`

The operator's ask for holding ``held_kw`` available for ``held_min`` minutes, in pence: pence per MW per hour x kW x minutes / 60,000.

### `call_budget_used(declaration: 'ComputeTurndownDeclaration', class_id: 'str', calls: 'Iterable[PastCall]', *, as_of: 'datetime') -> 'BudgetUse'`

The arithmetic of one SLA class's shared budget: every call naming any envelope of the class counts once. Reports; never refuses (`check_call` compares it with the limits).

### `call_cost_pence(price: 'PriceOffer | Unknown', *, reduction_kw: 'int', duration_min: 'int') -> 'Fraction | Unknown'`

The operator's ask for one called event, in pence: utilisation x kW x minutes / 60,000 (kW-minutes to MWh) plus the per-event fee. A component not charged counts 0; an unknown one (or an unknown price) makes the answer unknown, never zero.

### `check_call(declaration: 'ComputeTurndownDeclaration', call: 'ProposedCall', history: 'Sequence[PastCall]') -> 'CallCheck'`

Check the whole event ``[start, start + duration)`` against the declaration: validity, the state of every half-hour it touches, notice, hold, kW, exclusion, the concurrent cap and the retained floor (with the overlapping calls in ``history``), and each named SLA class's shared budget over every envelope of the class.

### `declaration_ref(declaration: 'ComputeTurndownDeclaration') -> 'DeclarationRef'`



### `declared_at_local(declaration: 'ComputeTurndownDeclaration', local_date: 'date', half_hour: 'int') -> 'OfferedAnswer | NotInForce'`

The state at a naive local half-hour (the load model's time basis: 48 half-hours a day).

### `deliverable_against(declaration: 'ComputeTurndownDeclaration', total_kw: 'int', it_load_kw: 'int') -> 'int'`

``total_kw`` limited so the IT load left is never below ``retained_it_floor_kw``.

### `deliverable_kw(envelope: 'TurndownEnvelope', duration_min: 'int', it_load_kw: 'int') -> 'int'`

One envelope alone: `turn_down_kw` of its curve. Combining envelopes is `stack_at`'s.

### `offered_at(declaration: 'ComputeTurndownDeclaration', instant: 'datetime') -> 'OfferedAnswer'`

The state at an aware ``instant`` inside the validity: an override's if one holds it, else the template cell's on the GB clock (the same lookup `resolve` uses).

### `pence_to_pounds(pence: 'Fraction') -> 'Fraction'`



### `price_basis_label(price: 'PriceOffer | Unknown') -> 'str'`

How a reader must label the price: indicative, firm (evidenced), or a placeholder.

### `resolve(declaration: 'ComputeTurndownDeclaration | TimeBase') -> 'ResolvedTimeline'`

Compile the availability onto UTC half-hours. Pure and deterministic; the declaration's ``resolved_hash`` is ``resolve(declaration).content_hash()``.

### `resolve_sla_evidence(sla_class: 'SlaClass', objects: 'Iterable[EvidenceObject]', *, include_synthetic: 'bool' = False) -> 'EvidenceObject | Unknown'`

The SLA document behind a class, resolved as an IC-4 ``service_level_agreement``. A self-issued record is never admitted; a synthetic one only when the caller asks. A class with no evidence answers ``unknown`` (IC-9 never requires an SLA document).

### `resolved_hash_of(draft: 'Mapping[str, Any]') -> 'str'`

The ``resolved_hash`` a draft declaration (JSON-mode mapping) must carry. The draft's other fields are ignored here; validating the declaration afterwards checks them all.

### `stack_at(declaration: 'ComputeTurndownDeclaration', instant: 'datetime', duration_min: 'int', it_load_kw: 'int') -> 'StackAnswer'`

The only way to combine envelopes. Takes the envelopes offered at ``instant`` in ``stacking.merit_order``; skips one whose exclusion group is already in the stack, or that cannot hold for ``duration_min``; converts each with `turn_down_kw` at ``it_load_kw``; and stops at ``max_concurrent_turn_down_kw`` and at the retained IT floor (`deliverable_against`). Summing curves instead would count alternatives twice and ignore the cap.

### `timeline_matches(declaration: 'ComputeTurndownDeclaration', timeline: 'ResolvedTimeline') -> 'bool'`

True when ``timeline`` is the declaration's compilation (checked by hash alone).

### `timeline_state_at(timeline: 'ResolvedTimeline', instant: 'datetime') -> 'OfferedAnswer'`

The state at ``instant``, read from the compiled timeline (no clock logic).

### `turn_down_kw(curve: 'AbsoluteCurve | RelativeCurve', duration_min: 'int', it_load_kw: 'int') -> 'int'`

kW of IT load the curve turns down for a hold of ``duration_min`` minutes when ``it_load_kw`` is running before the event. The first point whose hold covers the duration supplies it; beyond the longest hold the answer is 0. Never more than the running load: absolute ``min(kW, load)``; relative ``min(cap, floor(bp x load / 10,000))``.
